exercises.instruction: Choose the correct relative pronoun.
exercises.prompt: The scientist ___ discovered penicillin changed the history of medicine.
options: which
who
whose
whom
exercises.answer: who
exercises.explanation: 'Who' refers to people when it is the subject of the relative clause (the scientist discovered).

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct relative pronoun.
exercises.prompt: The research paper ___ she submitted won the departmental award.
options: who
whom
which
whose
exercises.answer: which
exercises.explanation: 'Which' refers to things (a research paper). 'That' would also be correct but is not offered here.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct relative pronoun for possession.
exercises.prompt: The student ___ thesis was published last year has now graduated.
options: who
which
whose
that
exercises.answer: whose
exercises.explanation: 'Whose' shows possession — the thesis belongs to the student.

exercises.instruction: Identify the sentence with an error.
options: The report that she submitted was excellent.
The doctor who treated me was excellent.
The book that I read it was fascinating.
The city where she grew up no longer exists.
exercises.answer: The book that I read it was fascinating.
exercises.explanation: Double pronoun error: 'it' is redundant because 'that' already represents the book. Remove 'it'.

exercises.instruction: Identify the sentence with the wrong relative pronoun.
options: The report which the team submitted was approved.
The engineer who designed the bridge retired.
The professor which taught me retired last year.
The moment when she realized the truth changed everything.
exercises.answer: The professor which taught me retired last year.
exercises.explanation: 'Which' cannot refer to people. Use 'who': 'The professor who taught me.'

exercises.instruction: In which sentence can the relative pronoun be omitted?
options: The man who called me was very polite.
The book that I borrowed was overdue.
The student whose laptop was stolen reported it.
The city where she was born is beautiful.
exercises.answer: The book that I borrowed was overdue.
exercises.explanation: 'That' is the object of 'borrowed' (I borrowed the book). Object pronouns can be omitted: 'The book I borrowed.'

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct relative pronoun for a time.
exercises.prompt: The year ___ the company was founded is still celebrated annually.
options: which
that
when
where
exercises.answer: when
exercises.explanation: 'When' is used to refer to times (the year, the moment, the day).

exercises.instruction: Choose the best sentence — the relative pronoun is correctly omitted.
options: The report submitted she won an award.
The report she submitted won an award.
The report which she submitted it won an award.
The report that submitted won an award.
exercises.answer: The report she submitted won an award.
exercises.explanation: Object relative pronoun omitted: 'The report [that] she submitted' — 'she' is the subject of 'submitted', so 'that' is the object and can be dropped.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct sentence using 'where'.
options: The hospital which I was born is still open.
The hospital where I was born is still open.
The hospital that I was born is still open.
The hospital who I was born is still open.
exercises.answer: The hospital where I was born is still open.
exercises.explanation: 'Where' = 'in which' for places. 'The hospital where' is correct for location.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct answer for: the correct relative pronoun.
exercises.prompt: The engineer ___ designed the new bridge won a national award.
options: whoing
that
whos
who
exercises.answer: who
exercises.explanation: 'Who' or 'that' — both correct for a person who is the subject of the relative clause.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct answer for: the correct relative pronoun for possession.
exercises.prompt: The company ___ products were recalled issued a full refund.
options: whoseing
did whose
whose
whoses
exercises.answer: whose
exercises.explanation: 'Whose' = possessive. The products belong to the company.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct answer for: the correct relative pronoun. The noun is a place.
exercises.prompt: The laboratory ___ the experiment was conducted has since been upgraded.
options: in which
wheres
where
whereing
exercises.answer: where
exercises.explanation: 'Where' = 'in which' for a place. Both are correct.

exercises.instruction: Can the relative pronoun be omitted? Write 'yes' or 'no' and explain why.
exercises.prompt: The professor ___ teaches us has written three books. Can 'who' be omitted?
options: noing
did no
no
nos
exercises.answer: no
exercises.hint: Is 'who' the subject or object of 'teaches'?
exercises.explanation: 'Who' is the subject of 'teaches' — subject relative pronouns cannot be omitted.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct answer for: the correct relative pronoun or write 'omit' if it can be dropped.
exercises.prompt: The book ___ I borrowed from the library was overdue.
options: thats
omit
that
which
exercises.answer: that
exercises.explanation: The relative pronoun is the object of 'borrowed' — 'that' or 'which' are correct, or it can be omitted.

exercises.instruction: Translate into English: "Pria yang menelepon saya kemarin adalah dokter."
exercises.prompt: Pria yang menelepon saya kemarin adalah dokter.
options: The man who called me yesterday is an doctor.
The man who called me yesterday is doctor.
The man who called me yesterday was a doctor.
The man who called me yesterday is a doctor.
exercises.answer: The man who called me yesterday is a doctor.
exercises.explanation: 'Yang' referring to a person (subject) → 'who' or 'that' in English.

exercises.instruction: Translate into English: "Mahasiswa yang laptopnya dicuri melapor ke keamanan."
exercises.prompt: Mahasiswa yang laptopnya dicuri melapor ke keamanan.
options: The student whose laptop was stolen reported it to security.
The student whose laptop was stolen reported to security.
The student which laptop was stolen reported it to security.
The student whose laptop is stolen reported it to security.
exercises.answer: The student whose laptop was stolen reported it to security.
exercises.explanation: 'Yang laptopnya' = 'whose laptop'. Use 'whose' for possession.

exercises.instruction: Translate into English: "Buku yang saya baca itu sangat menarik."
exercises.prompt: Buku yang saya baca itu sangat menarik.
options: The book I read was very interesting.
The book I read is very interesting.
The book I read it was very interesting.
The book which I read was very interesting.
exercises.answer: The book I read was very interesting.
exercises.explanation: 'Yang saya baca' = 'that I read' or omit 'that'. Do NOT add 'it' at the end.

exercises.instruction: Translate into English: "Kafe yang kami bertemu sudah tutup."
exercises.prompt: Kafe yang kami bertemu sudah tutup.
options: The café where we met is closed.
The café which we met has closed.
The café where we met has closed.
The café where we met have closed.
exercises.answer: The café where we met has closed.
exercises.explanation: Place noun (café) + 'yang' → 'where' in English.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct word.
exercises.prompt: The researcher ___ findings were published last month will give a talk today.
options: who's
whose
which
that
exercises.answer: whose
exercises.explanation: 'Whose' = possessive relative pronoun. 'Who's' = who is/has — completely different meaning.

exercises.instruction: Choose the sentence where the relative pronoun CAN be omitted.
options: The student who won the prize is my classmate.
The novel that she recommended is out of stock.
The café whose coffee I love has closed.
The year when she graduated was memorable.
exercises.answer: The novel that she recommended is out of stock.
exercises.explanation: 'That' is the object of 'recommended' (she recommended the novel) — object pronouns can be omitted.
